simple.meaning: אִמַּר (ʼimmar) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a lamb.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 6:9. The surrounding context includes offering, altar, priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אִמַּר (H563) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אִמַּר (ʼimmar) / H563 is traced through Ezra 6:9, Ezra 6:17, Ezra 7:17 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H563. immar [ אִמַּר ] noun masculine lamb (Assyrian immeru (also = child ; immertu , girl ; conjectures as to etymology Dl Prol. 28 Jen ZMG xiiii (1889), 203 ; ZA vii. 216 Schw Idioticon 114 ), אמריא ᵑ7 ; Syriac , Punic אמר , Palmyrene plural emphatic אמריא Lzb 220 Cooke Inscr. 120. 337 ; Arabic (loan-word ? compare Frä 107 , but also DHM VOJ i. 24 )); — plural אִמְּרִין , lambs , as sacrificial victims Ezra 6:9 , 17 ; 7:17 . אִנְבֵהּ see אֵב .
definitions.rootNote: (Aramaic) perhaps from 560 (in the sense of bringing forth);
